elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted warranty (b): "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Technical Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted warranty (a): "the Licensed Software will conform in all material respects to its Documentation" (Documentation is a defined term at 1.4).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software warranty runs only "for ninety (90) days following delivery"; no 12-month period is stated.
The services warranty runs only "for thirty (30) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall, at Licensee's option, repair or replace the non-conforming Licensed Software or Technical Support Services".
"...or refund the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the inserted language or elsewhere in the cited text.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code/virus warranty appears in the inserted language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "Licensor warrants that (a) for ninety (90) days following delivery, the Licensed Software will conform in all material respects to its Documentation"; the disclaimer is now prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN THIS ARTICLE VIX" and the nonconformity-correction sentence is prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED HEREIN", so the express warranty is not swallowed.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "(b) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Technical Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner." Technical Support Services are the services contemplated by this license-and-maintenance agreement.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall, at Licensee's option, repair or replace the non-conforming Licensed Software or Technical Support Services".
"...or refund the fees paid for them."

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: a 90-day Licensed Software conformance-to-Documentation warranty, a 30-day Technical Support Services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedies, all carved out of the AS IS disclaimer.

Preferred level fails on four elements: 12-month software period (drafted at 90 days), 90-day services period (drafted at 30 days), compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty (absent), and no-malicious-code warranty (absent). To reach preferred the drafter would need to extend the periods and add those two affirmative warranties.

Finding status 'deviation' is correct: the unamended text is the walk-away position (AS IS, all warranties disclaimed, express disclaimer that nonconformity to Documentation will be corrected), so a redline was warranted.

Minimality holds: only two narrow carve-out prefaces were added to the disclaimer and one concise warranty/remedy sentence inserted; no favourable existing language (including the Error Corrections obligation at p0093) was deleted and no survival tail, expense, notice-procedure or extra damages language was bolted on.

Intent preserved: the disclaimer otherwise survives intact, the Error Corrections covenant is unaffected, and both carve-outs remove the contradiction with the retained "NONCONFORMITY TO ITS DOCUMENTATION CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED" sentence. One drafting check: the new warranty must sit inside Article VIX or the cross-reference "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN THIS ARTICLE VIX" will dangle; the second carve-out uses "HEREIN", so align the two references.

Note (rationale, not a defect): the remedy election is drafted "at Licensee's option" rather than the model's Vendor option — this is Customer-favourable and within the remedy element, but expect Vendor pushback and be prepared to concede Vendor election.
